name: Trades business
description: A plumber, electrician, joiner, roofer or other tradesperson: the services, finished jobs as references, a price list and customers' questions, with facts about the area served, rates and the emergency line.

questions.question: Where do you work – which towns or how far from your base?
questions.help: For example "Brno and up to 40 km around". Customers check this before they call.

questions.question: Since which year have you been in business?
Do you charge a call-out fee? How much?
questions.help: An amount with the currency, e.g. 500 CZK or 40 EUR. Leave it empty if there is none.

questions.question: What is your hourly rate from?
questions.help: An amount with the currency; the price list holds the details.

questions.question: Do you offer an emergency service? Which number should people call?
questions.help: Leave it empty if you do not take emergency calls.

questions.question: What warranty do you give on your work?
questions.help: For example "24 months on labour, materials as the manufacturer". Check what your law requires as a minimum.

audit.message: Say where you work – customers outside your area should know before they call.
Fill in your phone number in Business details – most customers of a trade call.
Add the services you offer, each with what it includes and a price from.
Add at least one finished job with photos as a reference – customers want to see your work.
The price list has not changed for a year – check your rates and material prices.
Publish a privacy policy page – the enquiry form collects personal data; check what your law requires.

claude: Customers of a trade want three things fast: does this person do what I need, in my area, and how do I reach them – so the services, the area served and a phone number belong at the top of the home page, and the emergency line (if any) must be impossible to miss. Write in short, concrete sentences, like a tradesperson explaining the job, without marketing superlatives. Never invent references, photos, customer quotes, years of experience, certificates or prices – ask the owner for real finished jobs and publish them only with the customer's consent. Rates and the call-out fee are facts: state them once and let the price list carry the details. If a licence or registration may be required for the trade, note that it should be checked rather than claiming it.
